# fivenines_workflow_run (Data Source)

Reads a single workflow run with its per-step detail. The `fivenines_workflow_runs` index returns headers only, so a `failed` status there says a run broke but not where — `steps[].status` and `steps[].error_message` answer that.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The runs index returns headers only: `status = "failed"` there says a run
# broke, not where. Read the run itself for the per-step detail.
data "fivenines_workflow_runs" "failures" {
  workflow_id = fivenines_workflow.alert.id
  status      = "failed"
}

data "fivenines_workflow_run" "latest_failure" {
  workflow_id = fivenines_workflow.alert.id
  run_id      = data.fivenines_workflow_runs.failures.runs[0].id
}

output "failed_steps" {
  value = [
    for step in data.fivenines_workflow_run.latest_failure.steps :
    "${step.node_id}: ${step.error_message}" if step.status == "failed"
  ]
}

# The run-level message, set when a run fails between steps and no step
# explains it.
output "run_error" {
  value = data.fivenines_workflow_run.latest_failure.error
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `run_id` (Number) Run ID. Run IDs are not global: a run belonging to another workflow is not found here.
- `workflow_id` (Number) Workflow the run belongs to.

### Read-Only

- `completed_at` (String) When the run completed.
- `created_at` (String) When the run was created.
- `duration_seconds` (Number) Run duration in whole seconds. For a run still running this is the elapsed time so far, not a final duration.
- `error` (String) Run-level failure message. A run can fail between steps — a trigger that raised before any step row existed — in which case no step explains it and this is the only account of what happened.
- `resource_key` (String) The subject this run is for on a fan-out workflow (one run per host, guest, pool, ...). Null on a workflow that dispatches once.
- `started_at` (String) When the run started.
- `status` (String) Run status (running, completed, failed, cancelled).
- `steps` (Attributes List) Every node execution, in the order the engine created them. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--steps))
- `trigger_output_json` (String) What the trigger node emitted, as JSON. Decode with `jsondecode()`.
- `updated_at` (String) Last update timestamp.
- `workflow_version_id` (Number) The workflow version that was executed — not necessarily the currently published one.

<a id="nestedatt--steps"></a>
### Nested Schema for `steps`

Read-Only:

- `completed_at` (String) When the step completed.
- `created_at` (String) When the step was created.
- `duration_seconds` (Number) Step duration in seconds, millisecond resolution. Null — never 0 — while the step has not both started and finished.
- `error_message` (String) Set on a failed step. This is the answer to "which node broke".
- `id` (Number) Step ID.
- `node_id` (String) The node's ID within the version's execution graph (e.g. `trigger_1`).
- `node_type` (String) The node's type.
- `output_data_json` (String) Whatever the node produced, as JSON, its shape depending on `node_type`. Decode with `jsondecode()`.
- `started_at` (String) When the step started.
- `status` (String) Step status (pending, running, completed, failed, waiting, skipped). `waiting` is a node holding for a condition, not a failure; `skipped` means the graph routed around it.
